correctness.rationale: On the event that the observations lie in (0,1), the continuous likelihood has score n(t-F_n(t))/(t(1-t)) except at the sample knots. The score is positive before the first knot and negative after the last, and the log likelihood is convex between knots. Integration, also at 0 and 1, gives the exact centered profile. Changing variables on the two pieces gives the population log likelihood log(2)-1, including the limiting densities. On a compact interior subinterval apply Donsker and continuous integration (the bridge limit is continuous); the expected uniform truncation error on either end is at most the integral of 1/sqrt(t(1-t)) over that end, both before and after taking the limit. This proves convergence in C([0,1]) and a.s. existence of continuous improper integrals. The bridge area I has covariance t(1-t)/2 with B(t) and variance 1/12. Thus subtracting 6I t(1-t) leaves a Gaussian path independent of 6I, and after integration the conditional process is a fixed continuous function plus an independent linear tilt with a continuous slope law. A tie between distinct locations forces distinct subgradients of the convex supremum in the slope variable, an exceptional Lebesgue-null set. The compact argmax mapping at a unique maximum applies to every measurable selection. The transformation B(t) -> -B(1-t) reflects the profile, and its derivative at the midpoint is a nondegenerate normal variable. This proves both half-probabilities and nonconcentration. The uploaded script was inspected only; its finite diagnostics are not needed in this proof.
